newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA says Angola diamond-sharing deal close.
newsitem.headline: UNITA says Angola diamond-sharing deal close.

text.p: LUANDA, April 25 (Reuter) The Angolan state-owned diamond company and former rebels UNITA are just weeks away from signing a deal on how to share Angola's vast diamond deposits, a UNITA representative said on Friday.

"We have made some recent progress in the diamond talks and have reached some conclusions," said Isaias Samakuva, a top UNITA parliamentarian and the former rebel movement's main representative to U.N.-sponsored peace negotiations.
"There are still some minor details to be worked out but we should have an agreement in three to four weeks."
Diamond production in Angola is estimated to be worth around $1 billion a year with between $300 million and $600 million of production coming from UNITA-held areas.

UNITA (the Union for the Total Independence of Angola) entered into a power-sharing agreement with the government on April 11 that formally ended hostilities that started when the two sides went to war at independence from Portugal in 1975.
UNITA, though, still controls vast areas of the country -- some estimates are as high as 70 percent -- including most of the diamond producing areas.
A U.N. peacekeeping force of over 6,000 is overseeing continuing demilitarisation of UNITA, demobilisation of troops and extension of central government administration to all the country.

A deal legalising UNITA's current diamond holdings, including a formula spelling out how UNITA will participate with other concessionaires, including foreign ones, could be a key step in securing long term peace in the country, diplomats say.
Mining analysts said the power-sharing agreement provided a legal basis for the government diamond company, Endiama, and UNITA to sign a binding agreement.
One said that since UNITA was now part of the government it must recognize Endiama as the only state diamond company.

"UNITA is now part of the government," said the analyst. "They can't think of themseles as having the same rights to concession areas as Endiama, but that doesn't mean that UNITA can't be accommodated."
The analyst said there is a real possibility that part of the agreement could give UNITA permission to award concessions in certain parts of the country.
